gap: No retrieved study measures accuracy transfer across reasoning hop depth when training or RL-optimizing only on lower-hop instances. The only RL transfer evidence is cross-formalism (SQL/Cypher) with a +1.7% downstream KGQA gain and no per-hop breakdown, so the shallow-to-deep hop transfer hypothesis (H2) has no direct precedent or measurement convention.

evidence.quote: The model also demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization, improving performance on downstream tabular QA (TableBench: 8.5%) and knowledge graph QA (CR-LT-KGQA: 1.7%) without any QA-specific supervision.

why_unaddressed: The retrieved multi-hop KGQA systems report aggregate accuracy or a single-depth headline (CLAUSE emphasizes MetaQA-2-hop; EmbedKGQA reports overall Hits@1), and the RL work found transfers across query formalisms rather than reasoning depth. No retrieved paper reports a hop-depth transfer gap or controls for benchmark composition.
research_question: Does optimization restricted to 1-2 hop instances improve accuracy on 3+ hop queries, and is any measured transfer attributable to shared relations/entities rather than a reusable reasoning policy?
potential_experiment: Pre-register hop-depth splits on MetaQA (1/2/3-hop) and ComplexWebQuestions, train or RL-optimize only on 1-2 hop instances, and report Hits@1 per hop depth plus a transfer gap (deep minus shallow); include a construction analysis showing whether 3-hop test items reuse lower-hop relations/entities, and a mixed-hop control.
verification_required: Search for curriculum-learning and compositional-generalization work on multi-hop KGQA (including negative results where shallow training fails to transfer), and inspect benchmark construction papers for MetaQA/CWQ hop-depth composition; also verify whether any RL-for-KGQA work reports per-hop metrics.
